findings.decisionTitle: Asynchronous jobs: Amazon SQS, not Kafka
findings.decision: We use Amazon SQS queues for asynchronous work.
findings.decisionQuote: We use Amazon SQS queues for asynchronous work. Kafka was rejected: running and upgrading a Kafka cluster is more operational load than a six-person team can carry, and we do not need event replay today.
findings.pageTitle: ADR-002: Use SQS for asynchronous jobs, not Kafka

findings.workQuote: we keep the account tables in Postgres but write transactions to Couchbase
findings.explanation: Decision 65699:1 establishes PostgreSQL as the single system of record for all ledger and account data, including transactions; using Couchbase for transactions violates this rule.
findings.decision: PostgreSQL is the single system of record for all ledger and account data.
findings.decisionQuote: We use PostgreSQL as the single system of record for all ledger and account data. We will not introduce MongoDB or any other document database for ledger, transaction or account data.
findings.pageTitle: ADR-001: PostgreSQL as the system of record
